transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CIO - Venturo), Ethan Park (Infra), Lena Gomez (Security), Ravi Shah (ML)

Summary (auto-gen, maybe imperfect):
- Kickoff for POC to validate private-networking and residency.
- Discussed options: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink; some questions about cross-region and egress billing.
- Agreed next steps: share diagrams, sample traces, schedule deep-dive + benchmarks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Marta (CIO): Hi all, Marta here, CIO at Venturo Health. we're looking at inference infra for a clinical summarization product.
[00:16] Ethan (Infra): Ethan, infra, i'll own the networking bits.
[00:19] Lena (Security): Lena, security. focused on residency and egress.
[00:22] Ravi (ML): Ravi, ML lead, i'll cover workload shape.
[00:26] Priya (SE): Priya from Redwood, i'll run through benchmarks and test harness details.
[00:30] Alex: Great. quick agenda - scope success criteria, go over workload sizing, then networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regions, egress constraints, and finalize timeline. sound ok?
[00:38] Marta: Yep.

[02:12] Alex: So starting with success criteria, what would make this POC a win for Venturo?
[02:20] Marta: three things: response latency acceptable for live assist (p50 < 150ms ideally, p95 < 400ms), cost per 1k tokens within our target, and no data leaving EU region for PHI. also need audit logs and KMS integration.
[02:45] Ravi: i'll add quality regression - outputs must match our baseline prompts, we'll run a set of prompt evals.
[02:52] Priya: perfect, so success criteria = latency targets, cost envelope, residency/no-egress, and quality pass on eval set. we'll document that.

[05:05] Ethan: quick note on latency: if we do private deployment in our EU account with peering, p50 will be low. with hosted endpoints across regions we may see a hit due to cross-region hops.
[05:20] Alex: right. we typically recommend private deployment in-customer-VPC or dedicated capacity in same region; PrivateLink gives private connectivity without full peering.
[05:30] Ethan: what's the tradeoff again?
[05:33] Priya: VPC-peering = low-latency L3 connectivity, but requires route management and can be tricky across many accounts. PrivateLink = interface ENIs and endpoints, simplified security but potential added egress charges and slight extra latency. some customers prefer PrivateLink to avoid full routing changes.
[06:00] Marta: we are also constrained by procurement - we can't open peering across our prod account without infra review. PrivateLink may be faster to approve.

[07:10] Ravi: workload sizing - our current traffic plan for the pilot is average 12 QPS, spiky to 60 concurrent requests during peak, typical prompt length ~750 tokens inc. responses, average sequence length 1k tokens per request. batch size expected small (we need low latency).
[07:35] Priya: good, that maps to a low-latency config. for benchmarking we'll need realistic traces (timestamps, token counts). can you give sample logs?
[07:46] Ethan: yes we can provide anonymized trace for last 30 days, will scrub PHI.

[09:05] Alex: benchmark plan overview - Priya?
[09:08] Priya: plan is 3-phase: 1) baseline synthetic workloads to validate latency and throughput, 2) run trace-driven benchmarks using Venturo traces for 48-72 hours to catch caching/KV-cache warmups, 3) run a stability test for 1 week to observe autoscaling and cost. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, and per-token cost.
[09:40] Marta: timeline?
[09:42] Priya: kickoff this week for infra prep, network setup 3-5 business days, then benchmark run two weeks after kickoff. overall POC 3 weeks of active testing then 1-week wrap.
[09:55] Alex: so target decision point around 2026-12-01 if all goes well.

[11:10] Ethan: on PrivateLink specifics - we need to know the IP ranges, service name, if Redwood requires infra changes. Also whether endpoints will be interface endpoints in our account or in a shared services account.
[11:25] Priya: typically we ask for your AWS account IDs and VPC CIDRs. we can provide a service name for PrivateLink; you create the interface endpoints in your VPC. no peering change required. note that for large throughput PrivateLink can incur per-GB charges.
[11:42] Ethan: ok, we'll share accounts and CIDRs.

[12:30] Lena: data residency - we need assurance that tokens or embeddings never egress from eu-west-1. does Redwood support region pinning for inference?
[12:40] Alex: yes, we can pin model serving to a region. for hosted we have EU nodes and also private deployments where the runtime sits in your VPC in your account, so data never leaves.
[12:54] Lena: and encryption? KMS?
[12:57] Priya: KMS integrations supported - we can use customer-managed keys, and logs go to your CloudWatch or to a log-forwarder. audit logs and request-level metadata are available.

[14:00] Ravi: a question about KV cache - does that stay on the server side or can it be flushed/managed?
[14:07] Priya: KV cache is runtime-local per instance, we can expose APIs to evict or warm keys; for privacy-sensitive workloads cache eviction policies can be strict. also note sometimes transcription says K-V cash, ha.

[16:20] Marta: what about egress to external model registries or license checks? we need to ensure no outbound connections except to specific Redwood control plane endpoints.
[16:32] Alex: control plane traffic can be proxied via a restricted egress and we can white-list our control-plane IP ranges. for Private deployments, control plane traffic can be routed through a private link to our management endpoints, or in some enterprise deals we can run the control plane in your environment.

[18:45] Ethan: cross-region calls - we operate in eu-west-1 only for production. any cross-region fallback to us-east-1 is unacceptable. can Redwood guarantee region failover disabled?
[18:58] Priya: yes, we can set routing policies to region-only; fallbacks are opt-in. we'll put that in the config for the pilot.

[21:10] Ravi: metrics we need: per-route latency, per-secret KMS usage metrics, cost per token, model versioning traces.
[21:25] Priya: we'll provide dashboards and token-level cost breakdown. also can include trace ids to map model calls back to logs.

[23:00] Marta: legal wants SOC2 and ISO docs, and a data processing addendum if PHI is involved.
[23:10] Alex: we'll share SOC2 report and our standard DPA. Priya will attach security whitepaper.

[25:40] Ethan: performance benchmarks - for the synthetic test, what model variant do you recommend?
[25:46] Priya: we'll propose two model variants: an LLM-7B quantized variant for low-latency use, and a high-quality 13B variant as a comparison. we'll include CPU/GPU mapping and estimated throughput per GPU in the plan.

[27:12] Ravi: how do you handle autoscaling? can we limit concurrency per model to avoid tail-latency spikes?
[27:20] Priya: yes, autoscaling policies are configurable - scale by concurrency, tokens/sec, or queue depth. we can set max instances and warm pools for predictable latency.

[30:00] Alex: cost discussion: Private deployments have a fixed infra cost plus usage; hosted billed per token. Venturo's team, do you have a cost target per 1k tokens for the pilot?
[30:12] Marta: we are targeting under $4 per 1k tokens for the pilot workloads.
[30:20] Priya: we'll model that in the benchmark and show both quantized and fp16 profiles.

[33:00] Ethan: networking specifics - do you support VPC peering from our prod account to a Redwood-managed VPC, or do you require a shared services account?
[33:12] Alex: both supported. many customers prefer peering to a dedicated Redwood VPC in their region. others prefer PrivateLink from a shared services account. we'll provide diagrams for both.

[35:45] Lena: logs retention - we need 7 years? that's probably overkill, but at least 1 year and ability to export to our SIEM.
[35:55] Priya: export to S3/CloudWatch is supported; retention configurable. we'll confirm retention options.

[38:15] Ravi: benchmark acceptance criteria recap?
[38:20] Priya: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms, cost under $4/1k tokens, quality regression <= 5% delta on our eval metrics, no egress from eu-west-1, successful KMS integration, and passing security checklist.

[40:05] Marta: ok that sounds reasonable.

[42:30] Alex: let's confirm timeline again: this week share diagrams & account info; 3-5 days for network setup; week after that run trace-driven benchmarks; 1 week stability. target decision by 2026-12-01.
[42:50] Ethan: I'll get CIDRs and account IDs to Alex by Monday.
[43:00] Lena: I'll review DPA and confirm PHI constraints, will send notes by 2026-11-10.

[46:12] Priya: i'll follow up with bench plan and repo link - will need to install a small test agent or we can run from our harness hitting your PrivateLink endpoint.

[48:00] Marta: any blockers? procurement might want total cost estimate for dedicated infra.
[48:07] Alex: we can provide rough cost modeling after the initial traces; exact numbers will follow bench runs.

[50:30] Ravi: question about model updates and rollouts - can we pin to a model version for the POC?
[50:36] Priya: yes, pinning and controlled rollouts supported; we can do A/B or canary.

[52:20] Alex: ok great. thanks everyone. we'll send notes and next steps.
[52:27] Marta: thanks all.
[52:30] Meeting end.
